report:
Reviewed the complete body.elaboration claim, its three ordinary implementation entries, two ordinary tests and one explicit TODO test after fresh start and dependency recapture. The requirements are final types; semantic identities; materialized type-directed operations; and absence of source method syntax, unresolved names, inference variables, pending obligations and adjustment recipes from successful completed bodies. Successful output is the important qualification: diagnosed recovery trees are not successful elaboration.

Implementation inspection: expr.rs resolves paths into Res identities, fields into owner/index identities, inserts explicit built-in dereference nodes when accessing through references, and converts successful method selection to ResolvedCall with selected target and argument substitutions. The receiver adjustment helper in infer_ctx.rs inserts Ref nodes, while coerce_expr materializes NeverToAny and propagates it through block tails. Method failure becomes an error expression. The body completion boundary in InferCtx::finish asserts no pending obligations, live branches/tasks or unpublished wakes, fills every expression slot, and invokes finalize_typed_body. The associated finalizer recursively copies types, expressions, patterns, call target substitutions, statements and closure parameters into fresh storage, resolves inference representatives, rejects surviving InferVar, and substitutes expression slots. Finalize first converts unresolved inference into diagnosed recovery and terminally discharges obligations. These essential completion files now have direct associations, so their changes invalidate this review.

A concrete violation was reproduced during review: fn f(x: &[i32]) -> i32 { x[0usize] } yielded no diagnostics and a completed TyExprData::Index rather than the resolved Index call required by the captured indexing contract. The original anchor-associated test successful_indexing_body_contains_a_resolved_call failed with that exact node under cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test body_elaboration_review -- --nocapture. The unsuffixed preliminary probe x[0] instead diagnosed unconstrained integer inference and did not reproduce the violation. The coordinated minimal correction checks both operands, reports indexing elaboration is not supported yet, and gives the retained recovery node Ty::Error. Index/IndexMut lowering is explicitly TODO in the branch; this change does not claim to implement indexing. The new test indexing_reports_unsupported_until_call_elaboration_exists asserts the exact diagnostic on the suffixed reproducer, so the previously silent success cannot return unnoticed.

Test accounting: body_finalization_resolves_types_into_a_fresh_stash unifies an inference variable with i32, nests it in a tuple, finalizes, and asserts both that the original inference slot remains unchanged and that the completed nested element is i32. This directly verifies final type materialization, not all tree forms. The new indexing regression verifies honest rejection of a currently unsupported type-directed operation. The explicit TODO checking_body_elaboration remains deferred: its listed structural snapshot matrix for paths, fields, calls, generic substitutions, borrows, dereferences, coercions and recovery, exhaustive rejection of unresolved/live forms, and independent rustc exact-text comparisons are not established by these two tests. Its prerequisites are a completed per-form elaboration surface, structural observations/completion fixtures for those forms, and selected independent oracle slices. Accepting that explicit TODO does not turn it into passing functional coverage or claim that the full destination matrix exists. No N/A entries are present.

Captured extra context includes the review rules, architectural-foundations completed-body decision, typed IR guide, indexing claim, module declaration and test setup helpers/examples. After the correction I inspected the fresh source differences and complete new associated test. Commands executed: cargo fmt; cargo build (passed with existing warnings); the focused body_elaboration_review integration test (passed, one test). The original failing reproduction is described above; no full workspace test result or independent rustc comparison is claimed. The coordinator is responsible for the separately delegated post-codegen and Sage sanity reviews and final shared gate. No further edit is requested for this anchor; the explicit verification matrix and indexing support remain deferred as described.
